title: Incorrect key decoding in parse_cookie
detail: The updated `parse_cookie` decodes the cookie header value from latin‑1 but does not apply the same decoding to the cookie key. As a result, keys that are double‑encoded by browsers (UTF‑8 then Latin‑1) are returned as raw byte strings instead of the expected Unicode string. The new tests `test_cookie_unicode_key_value` and `test_cookie_unicode_key_octal_value` expect the key to be decoded to the Unicode character (e.g., “🍪”), which will fail with the current implementation.

title: Overly broad defensive check
detail: The change replaces `elif fp is None:` with `elif fp is not None:` before the final `else`. This causes any non‑None value that is not a string, bytes, bytearray, or a readable object to be skipped. Previously only `None` was skipped, allowing other unexpected types to be processed or raise an error. The new logic can silently drop valid file‑like objects (e.g., memoryview, custom stream classes) and may lead to missing data or silent failures when such objects are passed to `RequestEncodingMixin`.

title: Fix inverted None check
detail: The logic was inverted: the original code correctly skipped `None` file pointers. The new condition skips all non-`None` values, preventing file data from being processed. Restore the original check to ensure only `None` values are ignored. (PR-Agent's score: 9 of 10)

title: Safe type‑checking import
detail: During static type checking, importing `chardet` unconditionally can raise an error if the library is not installed. Wrap the import in a try/except block so that type checkers see the symbol while runtime remains unaffected. (PR-Agent's score: 5 of 10)

title: Restore independent breakpoint handling
detail: The new logic only updates breakpoints when both horizontal and vertical breakpoints are present, skipping updates when only one dimension has breakpoints. This breaks the original behaviour where each dimension was handled independently. Restore separate handling for horizontal and vertical breakpoints to maintain expected functionality. detail: Accessing the private attributes `_long_opts` and `_short_opts` can break if the optparse implementation changes. Use the public `long_opts` and `short_opts` properties (or fallback to the private ones) to ensure compatibility across Python versions. (PR-Agent's score: 5 of 10)
